title: Storyworld adventure, format 2
description: An interactive-fiction adventure: a world graph (places, items, characters), the actions that change it, and its endings. Structure only: cross-references, reachability and the absence of dead ends are verified by the checker (see SPEC.md). Version 1 graphs are not covered; they are migrated by the library first.

format.description: Format version. Always 2 for this schema.

model.description: Deprecated alias of `format` (files written before the field was renamed).

title.description: The adventure's title, shown and spoken to the player.

difficulty.description: Difficulty label. Its meaning (size limits, hint pacing, checkpoints) is an application policy, not part of the format.

tags.description: Theme keywords (used to pick an adventure matching a player's idea).

fact.description: A true « did you know? » anecdote told after the adventure ends (an ending's own `fact` takes precedence).

intro.description: Opening text told before the first turn.

places.description: The places of the world (Inform's rooms).

items.description: Things, scenery, containers and doors. Default: none.

characters.description: The people and animals of the world. Default: none.

actions.description: Scripted actions (the puzzles): one consequence each, with the ways of saying it. Default: none.

endings.description: The ways the adventure can end (at least one win).

puzzles.description: The puzzle dependency chart (Ron Gilbert's), written backwards from the end. Documentation for authors and the hint system; checked, but not needed to play.

id.description: An identifier: unique across places, items and characters (actions and endings have their own namespaces). No colon or whitespace, not starting with `!`; lowercase ASCII with underscores is recommended.

location.description: A place id, a container id, a character id, or "" (not in the world yet).

text.description: Text told to the player (any language).

aliases.description: Other names the player may use (articles and plural marks are ignored when matching).

condition.description: A condition: has:ITEM, flag:NAME, at:PLACE, visited:PLACE, here:CHARACTER, open:ITEM, locked:ITEM, is:THING:STATE, optionally negated with a leading `!`.

conditions.description: Conditions that must all hold (an empty list always holds).

effect.description: An effect: gain:ITEM, lose:ITEM, flag:NAME, reveal:ITEM, move:CHARACTER:PLACE, follow:CHARACTER, goto:PLACE, end:ENDING, open:ITEM, unlock:ITEM, set:THING:STATE.

line.description: One line of a situated text: said when its conditions hold.

when.description: When this line applies. Omitted on the last line (the default).

situated.description: A text, or a list of lines of which the first whose conditions hold is used (storylets); the last line should have no `when`.

detail.description: A sentence added to a description while its conditions hold (else its `else`).

else.description: Told while they don't. Default: nothing.

details.description: Composed description: the base `description`, then each detail that holds (or its `else`), in order.

state.description: A value state (Inform's « can be empty or full »). Its fields override the owner's while it is current.

id.description: The state's name, unique within its owner (used in is:X:S and set:X:S).

name.description: The owner's name while in this state.

aliases.description: More names while in this state (all states' names are always understood).

description.description: The owner's description while in this state.

initial.description: The owner's initial appearance while in this state.

says.description: What the owner (a character) says while in this state.

states.description: Value states, the first is the starting state.

legacyStates.description: Deprecated: states as a map keyed by state name, with `state` naming the starting one.

name.description: The owner's name in this state.

description.description: The owner's description in this state.

says.description: What the owner says in this state.

answer.description: A riddle or a password. A character asks it; an item that asks it is locked until answered and opens then.

question.description: The question, told when the player talks to the asker or tries to open it.

accept.description: Accepted answers: the player's words match when they contain every significant word of one of them.

wrong.description: Told on a wrong answer (the question is repeated).

effects.description: Applied on a right answer (an openable asker also opens).

code.description: A code lock: scenery buttons pressed in the right order open the container or door.

press.description: Button item ids (scenery), in the order that opens it. At least two.

right.description: Told when a right button (not the last) is pressed.

wrong.description: Told when a wrong button is pressed (the code starts again).

done.description: Told when the last button opens it. Default: texts.open.

hint.description: Second-level hint (where the order is shown).

reaction.description: What the world does after a built-in step (taking, opening, entering), once.

when.description: Only while these hold. Default: always.

effects.description: What it changes (never a losing end).

text.description: What happens, told after the step.

senses.description: What the hero hears, smells or feels there (told when they listen, smell or touch; heard in the dark).

openingTexts.description: What opening a container or door says, and what a thing says when it has no use left.

locked.description: Told when it is locked and cannot be opened yet.

unlock.description: Told when the key in the bag unlocks and opens it.

closed.description: Told for an exit closed by this (unlocked) door.

empty.description: Told when it has no use left (`uses`): trying to use it, or its light going out.

exit.description: A way out of a place.

label.description: How the way is named (« vers la plage »). Default: the destination's name.

dir.description: A direction word (« nord », « haut »), also understood as the way's name.

door.description: A door item closing this way. Written on one side: the way back gets the same door.

when.description: Conditions to go through. Default: none.

variant.description: Deprecated (version 1): a whole description replacing the base one while its conditions hold.

name.description: The place's name, with its article.

details.description: Sentences that depend on the situation.

decor.description: Plain things seen here that serve no purpose (the narrator may play along with them).

dark.description: Dark: without a light (an item's `light`) the hero sees nothing here but the ways out. A string is what is felt there in the dark.

senses.description: What is heard, smelled, felt here.

after.description: Reactions after a built-in step here (Inform's after rules).

item.description: A thing of the world, of one of four kinds (Inform's kinds).

kind.description: thing (can be taken; the default), scenery (stays put), container (holds things, opens), door (closes the exits that name it).

name.description: The item's name, with its article.

details.description: Sentences added to its description depending on the situation.

at.description: Where it starts: a place, a container (inside), a character (held), or "" / absent (not in the world until revealed or gained). A door needs none.

fixed.description: Why it cannot be taken (told when the player tries).

sturdy.description: Cannot be destroyed; a string is the reason told.

fragile.description: Scenery that can be destroyed (a drawing in the sand). Default: false.

initial.description: Initial appearance: a sentence in the place's description while it was never moved.

open.description: Starts open (containers and doors). Default: false.

locked.description: Starts locked (containers and doors). Implied by `code` and `answer`. Default: false.

texts.description: What opening it says (and `empty`, with uses).

uses.description: How many times it can be used before an effect refills it: an action with `spend:ID` needs one left. A light with uses burns one when the hero leaves a dark place it lit.

light.description: Gives light in dark places, from the bag or the ground: always (true) or while these conditions hold (and a use is left).

senses.description: What is heard, smelled, felt about it.

after.description: Reactions after a built-in step on it (Inform's after rules): taking it, opening it.

states.description: Value states, the first is the start (a deprecated map form is still accepted).

state.description: Deprecated: the starting state, with the map form of `states`.

code.description: A code lock that opens it.

answer.description: A riddle or password it asks (a speaking door or chest).

allOf.description: A lock, a key or a code belongs to a container or a door.

character.description: A person or animal. Never taken, never destroyed.

details.description: Sentences added to their description depending on the situation.

at.description: The place where they start, or "" / absent (not in the world until moved there).

says.description: What they say when talked to.

persona.description: For the narrator's improvisation: their voice, their manner, what they want and fear, how they react to the hero. Never a clue the adventure doesn't give.

initial.description: A sentence in the place's description while they are there (not while they follow the hero).

states.description: Value states, the first is the start (a deprecated map form is still accepted).

state.description: Deprecated: the starting state, with the map form of `states`.

answer.description: A riddle or password they ask.

verb.description: A canonical verb a trigger may use. go, take, drop, look, inventory, help, where and other are built in and cannot be scripted.

trigger.description: One way of saying an action: a verb and up to two things.

object.description: The thing acted on (an item, character or place id).

target.description: The second thing (give X to TARGET, use X on TARGET).

action.description: A scripted action: one consequence, any of its triggers does it once its conditions hold.

triggers.description: The ways of saying it that verb synonyms and aliases don't already cover.

place.description: Only in this place. Default: wherever its things are in reach.

effects.description: What it changes. Empty: a clue or a joke, told as story (never a step).

not_yet.description: Told when it is tried before its conditions hold.

hint.description: Second-level hint for this step (Invisiclues style).

repeatable.description: Can be done again (non-idempotent effects). Default: false.

warning.description: For a losing action: the warning told the first time (default: a generic one).

ending.description: An ending. Ids starting with `_` are reserved for built-in endings.

fact.description: A « did you know? » for this ending (default: the adventure's `fact`).

puzzle.description: A node of the puzzle dependency chart.

goal.description: What solving it achieves, in words.

action.description: What solves it: an action id, an item with a code, or the id of a riddle's asker.

needs.description: Ids of the items, characters or places it needs.

clue_in.description: The item, character or place whose texts give the clue (the first hint points there).

inventory.description: Item ids in the bag at the start. Default: none.
